title: Group Chat and Locker
premise: Rafael Iversen, a debate champion at Westgate High, has perfected the art of saying 'I'm fine' — about his parents' crumbling marriage, his scholarship pressure, and the group chat that's gone strangely quiet. When his best friend Priya vanishes, leaving only her locker keys and a half-deleted message thread, Rafael and his found family of misfit teammates must decode what she left behind while pretending everything is normal for the state championship. As the search intensifies, loyalties fracture: someone in the friend group knew where Priya was going and said nothing, and telling the truth might destroy the team — and Priya's trust — forever. In the end, Rafael wins the debate trophy he no longer cares about, loses the final game that matters more, and finds Priya alive but changed, choosing truth over loyalty and discovering that his real family is the one that stayed to look for her.
about_author: Sable Marchetti is a former high school debate coach who spent six years watching teenagers say true things in the safest possible words. She writes from a converted garage in Portland, Oregon, surrounded by abandoned group chats she still can't bring herself to leave.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He wins a regional debate qualifier with a flawless closing argument, then comes home to a silent dinner where his parents perform civility like a losing motion. He texts the group chat 'all good here?' and gets read receipts from only two of five friends. Emotional beat: the gap between public victory and private dread.

chapters.title: The Locker Keys
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Monday morning, Priya doesn't show. Her locker stands open, cleaned out except for a single keyring taped inside with Rafael's name on masking tape. The coach says she transferred; the office has no paperwork. Marcus pockets the keys before anyone else sees them. Emotional beat: the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Read at 11:47 PM
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The friend group reconvenes in person for the first time in weeks, scrolling their chat history for clues. Priya's last message — 'does anyone actually check this thing?' — was read by all five of them and answered by none. Guilt lands differently on each of them. Emotional beat: collective complicity in small abandonments.

chapters.title: What the Key Opens
chapters.summary: Devon's POV. The keys fit nothing at school, nothing at Priya's house. Devon, the team's quiet researcher, identifies them as storage-unit keys across town. They agree to go Saturday — after practice, because championships are next month and Coach Okafor is watching attendance. Emotional beat: loyalty measured in scheduling compromises.

chapters.title: Unit 114
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Inside the storage unit: boxes of Priya's mother's belongings, eviction notices, and a notebook documenting that Priya had been living between friends' couches for two months without any of them noticing. Rafael realizes she asked each of them for help in ways too small to hear. Emotional beat: shame disguised as determination.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Jules's POV. Debate semifinals arrive; Rafael phones it in and advances anyway. Jules covers for him with the coach, lying fluently — a skill she hates having. Meanwhile police classify Priya as a voluntary runaway, sixteen and 'known to be troubled.' Emotional beat: the machinery of institutions smoothing over a missing girl.

chapters.title: Someone Knew
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus admits to Rafael, alone, that Priya told him three weeks ago she was 'getting out' — and he assumed she meant college applications. He never passed it on. He makes Rafael swear not to tell the others yet. Emotional beat: the weight of being trusted with the wrong secret.

chapters.title: The Notebook's Last Page
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Hidden in the notebook's binding: an address in another city and a name — 'D. Reyes.' Devon goes pale when they see it; Reyes is Devon's estranged older brother, who left home years ago under circumstances the family never discusses. Emotional beat: the mystery turns inward.

chapters.title: Interrogation, Friendly Format
chapters.summary: Devon's POV. The group corners Devon with the gentleness of people who've watched too many crime shows. Devon insists they haven't spoken to their brother in four years — then falters, admitting Priya called them last month asking how to reach him. Devon didn't answer the call. Emotional beat: fear wearing the mask of silence.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth, Round One
chapters.summary: Jules's POV. The group fractures over whether to tell the police about Reyes. Marcus argues it will get Devon's family investigated for nothing; Jules argues Priya is more important than anyone's comfort. Rafael, the debater, can't build the case — both sides are right. Emotional beat: the theme made literal.

chapters.title: The Final Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The basketball team — Marcus, Jules, and Priya's old teammates — plays the rival school where Reyes reportedly lives. Between quarters, Marcus spots a man in the stands matching Devon's description of his brother. He loses track of the score entirely. Emotional beat: the game stops mattering mid-game.

chapters.title: Following D. Reyes
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael and Marcus tail Reyes after the game to a diner, where they see him meet a teenage girl through the window — but the angle is wrong, the light is wrong, and they can't confirm it's Priya before he drives off. They get a partial plate. Emotional beat: hope that feels almost cruel.

chapters.title: The Plate Comes Back
chapters.summary: Devon's POV. The partial plate traces to a Reyes cousin in Fairview, forty miles out. Devon finally breaks: they call their brother directly, against everyone's advice, and he hangs up on them — but not before Devon hears a second voice in the background, young, laughing. Emotional beat: terror and relief tangled together.

chapters.title: State Semifinals
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael debates the state semifinal on autopilot and wins on a technicality, feeling nothing. His mother attends for the first time all season and cries in the parking lot about his father, asking Rafael to be 'the strong one.' He realizes he's been cast as the family's closer. Emotional beat: inheritance of other people's burdens.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Explodes
chapters.summary: Jules's POV. Jules, exhausted by secrets, tells the whole group about Marcus's admission — that he knew Priya was leaving. The chat becomes a battlefield: accusations, defenses, screenshots. Devon quietly leaves the chat. For the first time, the found family looks like it might not survive the case. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon and a wound.

chapters.title: Fairview
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael, Marcus, and Jules drive to Fairview without telling adults, using the championship road trip as cover. They find the cousin's house, the car, and — through a kitchen window — Priya, alive, setting a table. She sees them and her face collapses into something between fury and relief. Emotional beat: finding her is not the same as understanding her.

chapters.title: Why She Left
chapters.summary: Priya's POV (first time). Priya tells them everything: her mother's eviction, the couch-surfing shame, and why she chose Reyes — a stranger with a spare room — over the friends she loved: because asking them would have made her a burden, and staying invisible felt safer than being seen struggling. Emotional beat: the loneliness at the center of a crowded group chat.

chapters.title: The Argument She Wins
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya refuses to come home; she's enrolled in a Fairview school, working at the cousin's shop, stable for the first time in a year. Rafael tries to debate her back and loses — genuinely, completely — to the best argument he's ever heard. Instead he offers her what she actually needs: the truth told to the adults, on her terms. Emotional beat: love means losing gracefully.

chapters.title: Telling Everyone
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The group returns and faces the fallout: parents, police, Coach Okafor, Devon's furious family. Marcus publicly owns his silence at a team meeting, and the apology costs him his captaincy. Devon rejoins the chat with one message: 'next time, we answer.' Emotional beat: accountability as the price of staying.

chapters.title: The Final
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. State championship final. Rafael debates with everything he's learned — about what arguments are for — and wins the title, then dedicates it to 'someone who taught me when to stop debating.' His parents watch, holding hands uncertainly, beginning their own harder conversation. Emotional beat: winning the thing that doesn't matter, honestly.

chapters.title: The Last Game
chapters.summary: Jules's POV. The basketball team plays its true final game without Marcus as captain, and loses by two. Nobody minds. Priya video-calls from Fairview during the handshake line, and the whole team crowds the phone, shouting. Emotional beat: defeat shared is better than victory hoarded.

chapters.title: Group Chat, Renamed
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, epilogue. Summer. The group chat is renamed 'Answer Within 24 Hours.' Priya visits every other weekend; Rafael's parents are in honest, painful counseling; Devon and Reyes exchange careful letters. Rafael types 'all good here?' — and this time, all five answer within a minute. Emotional beat: fine, redefined as something you build together.
